solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cries, opening post: lucky win here?

indicators.note: the word for cries splits open the word for a post, sitting inside it

parts.note: a post is a stake driven into the ground
to cry is to weep, so cries are weeps

explanation.surface: Someone sobbing as a fence post goes in, oddly followed by a question about where luck pays off.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery-style draw in which prizes go to whoever holds the drawn tickets, so any win there is pure luck.

clue.text: Bribes singers briefly

definitions.meaning: small payments or concessions made to keep someone quiet
a clipped plural short form of sopranos, the highest voices

explanation.surface: A short note that some vocalists have been paid off.
explanation.definitionFit: A sop is a small concession or payment given to placate someone, much like a bribe.

clue.text: Hear the district nurses got to ground safely

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so these words cradle the answer within them

explanation.surface: An instruction to listen as the local nursing service brings someone down to the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' looks like the district's staff but signals letters held inside heAR THE District.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical circuit connected to ground has been made safe by that connection, the British term for grounding.

clue.text: Dependant's pathetic story?

parts.note: something pathetic is poor or inadequate
a relation is a telling or narrative, a story

explanation.surface: A sob story told by someone who relies on another.
explanation.walkthrough: Relation here means a telling, as in the relation of events.
explanation.definitionFit: A family member who is less well off and relies on wealthier kin is the classic dependant.

clue.text: Child hides each panic originally — it pours out

indicators.note: the word for a child conceals the following letters inside it

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word panic

explanation.surface: A child hiding as panic first sets in, with something spilling out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it pours out' reads like panic spreading, but it is the definition: a kitchen vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel with a spout from which brewed tea is poured into cups.

clue.text: Shoot sweet-sounding plover

parts.note: to shoot game is to kill it

indicators.note: sounding says the word for sweet is heard rather than spelt, giving a same-sound animal

parts.note: a sweet person is a dear

explanation.surface: A hunter fires at a bird with a pleasant call.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American bird of the plover family, named for its shrill call.

clue.text: Elegant fowl has no range

indicators.note: has no says the word for range is taken out of the bird's name

parts.note: a chicken is a domestic fowl
ken is range of knowledge, as in beyond one's ken

explanation.surface: A smart bird that has no room to roam.
explanation.walkthrough: KEN means range only in the sense of knowledge or sight, as in 'beyond my ken'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic describes stylish, fashionable elegance in dress or manner.

clue.text: Crop top beneath fur? Not I!

indicators.note: in a down clue the garment word sits below the fur word
not I says the letter I is dropped from the word for fur

parts.note: fur is an animal's hair
a vest is an undershirt, a top

explanation.surface: Someone denying they put a cropped top under a fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crop top' looks like one garment; Crop is the definition and top is VEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The gathered crop of a season is the harvest, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Who comes after the Romans? Some rural types

definitions.meaning: in Mark Antony's speech, Friends, Romans is followed by the third group addressed
country dwellers, people who live and work in the countryside

explanation.surface: A history question about Rome's successors, answered by talk of country folk.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half quotes Shakespeare's Julius Caesar: 'Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears.'
explanation.definitionFit: People from the countryside, rural dwellers as opposed to townsfolk.

clue.text: Going into a Bible story, teacher is not to be condemned

indicators.note: the teacher word enters the story word, placed inside it

parts.note: a parable is a moral tale such as those told in the Gospels
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A lecturer delving into scripture is judged blameless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forgivable or excusable does not deserve condemnation.

clue.text: Hamburger perhaps almost a deception

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is cut off the deception word

parts.note: a fraud is a deception or swindle

explanation.surface: A burger that is nearly a con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamburger' is not the sandwich but a person from Hamburg, here a German woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A German married woman or wife, so a woman from Hamburg is an example.

clue.text: Hoodlum, one in a suit, who may be better than he appears

definitions.text: who may be better than he appears

parts.note: a rough is a violent thug or hooligan
diamonds is one of the four suits in a pack of cards, and a diamond is a card of it

explanation.surface: A thug dressed in a suit may be nicer than he looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for someone with a coarse manner but a good heart underneath.

clue.text: Woman and others collect fuel for robbers' sanctuary

parts.note: she stands for a woman

indicators.note: the woman and others gather the next words into their midst

parts.note: the rest are the others
wood is burned as fuel

explanation.surface: A woman and her companions gathering firewood.
explanation.walkthrough: The legendary band were outlaws rather than robbers, but the definition is near enough.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nottinghamshire woodland where Robin Hood's outlaw band hid, in English legend.

clue.text: Undisciplined, disliking untidiness? Grow up!

parts.note: to be off something is to have gone off it, to dislike it
a mess is untidiness
to age is to grow older

explanation.surface: A rebellious youngster who can't abide a messy room is told to mature.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician straying from the party line is undisciplined in the political sense.

clue.text: Doctor breaks tool in tricky operation

indicators.note: the doctor letters break into the tool word, splitting it

parts.note: a file is a tool for smoothing
DD is Doctor of Divinity

explanation.surface: A surgeon snaps an instrument during a difficult procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' and 'operation' suggest surgery; Doctor is DD.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddle is a swindle or dodge, a dishonest piece of trickery.

clue.text: Ham, for one, and egg — crazy about it

indicators.note: the word for crazy goes around the egg

parts.note: potty is British slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Ham and eggs, with someone mad about the dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' is not meat but Ham Peggotty, a character in Dickens's David Copperfield.
explanation.definitionFit: Ham is one of the family of that surname in Dickens's David Copperfield.

clue.text: One that kept leading Achilles by the ears was our master

indicators.note: by the ears says the phrase is judged by its sound rather than spelling

parts.note: a master who teaches us has taught us

explanation.surface: A tribute to a teacher, mixed with Greek legend.
explanation.walkthrough: In Alice in Wonderland the Mock Turtle's master was called this 'because he taught us'. Zeno's paradox has Achilles never overtaking it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Zeno's paradox, a slow reptile with a head start is never caught by swift Achilles.

clue.text: In the long run, earl's child follows revolutionary

indicators.note: the title for an earl's child comes after the revolutionary

parts.note: Jean-Paul Marat was a leader of the French Revolution
an earl's younger son or daughter is styled the Honourable, abbreviated Hon

explanation.surface: Eventually, a nobleman's offspring takes after a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the long run' reads as an idiom for eventually; the definition is just 'long run'.
explanation.definitionFit: A road race of about 26 miles, the longest standard running event.

clue.text: Very keen to assume English parents' duties

indicators.note: to assume is to take on, so the keen word takes the letter inside

parts.note: raring, as in raring to go, means very eager

explanation.surface: Someone eager to take on the role of mum and dad.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing up children is what mothers and fathers do.

clue.text: Conscious about daughter that's liable to pop up

indicators.note: the conscious word goes around the daughter letter

parts.note: to be conscious of is to be aware

explanation.surface: A parent alert to their daughter, who may suddenly appear.
explanation.definitionFit: Software showing advertisements, often in windows that suddenly appear on screen.

clue.text: An excitement as queen leaves nest

indicators.note: the queen letter departs from the excitement word

parts.note: a thrill is a surge of excitement
R stands for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A thrill felt as the monarch departs her home.
explanation.definitionFit: A mound built by insects as their colony home, hence a nest.

clue.text: Extremely coarse, proper grass

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme letters, first and last, of coarse

parts.note: real means genuine, proper

explanation.surface: A grass described as truly rough.
explanation.definitionFit: Grains such as wheat and oats come from cultivated grasses.

clue.text: Instinctive representation of feet as hot?

parts.note: pants is slang for rubbish, so the phrase seat of the, made into pants, becomes the words feet as hot

explanation.surface: A picture of someone's sweltering feet.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as wordplay is SEAT OF THE with PANTS (rubbish) as a signal to rearrange, giving 'feet as hot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by the seat of one's pants means relying on instinct rather than plans.

clue.text: Don't accept fate: it's about to be rejected

indicators.note: rejected means these letters are thrown out of the word for fate

parts.note: destiny is fate

indicators.note: about means the word it's is turned round

explanation.surface: Advice not to resign yourself to fate, since it is about to be turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ITS into STI; 'to be rejected' takes STI out of DESTINY.
explanation.definitionFit: To refuse to accept something or to refuse to believe a claim.

clue.text: Keen, suggesting a tanner?

parts.note: a tanner was an old British sixpence, written VI D in Roman numerals plus d for pence

explanation.surface: Someone eager, hinted at by an old coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner is the pre-1971 British sixpenny coin, written 6d.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager or enthusiastic, as in an avid reader.

clue.text: Donate books in attractive cover to intimate

parts.note: to donate is to give

indicators.note: in places the books inside the attractive word
the attractive word acts as a cover wrapped around the books

parts.note: nice means pleasant, attractive
OT is the Old Testament, books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Giving away books in a pretty dust jacket to someone close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intimate' is the verb, to announce, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To give notice is to announce formally, and to intimate is to make known.

clue.text: Wetland plant has no small advantage

indicators.note: has no says the small letter is dropped from the plant

parts.note: sedge is a grasslike plant of marshes

explanation.surface: A marsh plant without any small benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the edge over a rival means holding a slight advantage.

clue.text: Man will wheel camera platform, getting hit on stage

parts.note: he'll is the contraction of he will, a man will
O is round like a wheel
a dolly is a wheeled platform for a film camera

explanation.surface: A man pushing a camera rig on set gets struck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' is a success, not a blow: a hit Broadway musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running Broadway musical, a smash success on stage.
